question: Should the OpenGrep workflows permit retries while executable installer bytes are streamed directly into Bash, or require an atomic download-then-execute boundary?
rationale: This is a security-sensitive CI execution path, and retaining the existing streaming handoff trades a smaller patch against retry integrity that static tests cannot settle.

options.title: Require atomic execution
options.body: Download the pinned installer completely into a temporary file, then execute it once after curl reports success.

options.title: Accept streaming retries
options.body: Keep the pipe-to-Bash implementation and explicitly accept partial-output retry behavior after reviewing live failure proof.

recommendation.title: Require atomic execution
recommendation.body: Download the pinned installer completely into a temporary file, then execute it once after curl reports success.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the OpenGrep workflow surface and are the strongest history-backed owner for its installer trust boundary.
